title: A hawkish Federal Reserve won’t deliver bullish hikes
gist: Oxford Economics argues the Fed's hawkish turn under Kevin Warsh is unlikely to produce 'bullish rate hikes' with falling bond yields, since such episodes require fast-adjusting prices and wages more typical of emerging markets. Stickier post-pandemic US inflation could force more hikes, while fiscal profligacy and AI productivity add upward pressure on long-term yields.

insights.so_what: Don't position for long-end yields falling just because the Fed turns hawkish.
